metadata.title: Allocating AI Translation Compute for Marginal Educational Access
metadata.description:
This standalone research report develops a reproducible global portfolio model for allocating AI-assisted adaptation of open educational resources according to additional comfortable, usable access. It joins typed population evidence to exact language, variety, script, territory, learner, curriculum, accessibility, and overlap profiles; evaluates natural-language and evidence-bounded interlanguage architectures; assigns stage-specific first products; and separates measured evidence from operational planning policy.

Version 1.1 contains 477 population observations and 83 source records, a globally recalled profile universe, intensive needs studies, 100 concrete commissioning profiles, a Top-100 needs layer, an interlanguage-overlap crosswalk, and an audited Indonesian-program compute anchor. The operational Top 10 begins with Bangla shared-source residuals, Telugu, Odia, Bhojpuri, and Hausa. Bahasa Indonesia, Mainland Simplified Chinese, and Japanese are explicitly evaluated on the same basis rather than omitted.

Research synthesis, analysis, drafting, and reproducibility work used OpenAI Codex gpt-5.6-sol, Ultra. Source authors and public-project contributors retain their original credits. First-party paper and data are licensed CC BY 4.0; first-party code is MIT licensed; third-party works retain their own terms.
metadata.notes: Standalone publication with version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22217113 and a dedicated public GitHub repository. PAPER.pdf is the required default landing-page preview. The record contains mixed first-party CC BY 4.0 material, MIT-licensed code, and separately noticed third-party facts or references; file-level notices control. Token counters are accounting units, not FLOPs, energy, GPU time, monetary cost, or weekly-plan consumption. Nested Indonesian accounting views must not be added.
